en: O Cakrapāṇi, whose abode is the glorious ocean, whose holy form is resplendent with the jewels upon the coils of the lord of serpents! (Alternative reading: O you whose holy form is adorned by the jewels upon the coils of the lord of serpents!)
O Lord of Yogis, eternal refuge, boat for the ocean of worldly existence, Lakṣmī-Nṛsiṃha, grant me the support of Your hand! 1.
O Lord whose stainless splendor causes the lotus-feet of Brahmā, Indra, Rudra, the Maruts, and the Sun to be struck by the tips of their crowns;
O royal swan upon the lotuses of Lakṣmī’s shimmering breasts!
O Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha, grant me the support of Your hand. 2.
Of him whose body hairs were utterly scorched by the rows of flames from the terrifying forest-fire of saṃsāra (or, according to a variant reading, from the distressing forest-fire of saṃsāra).
O Lakṣmī-Nṛsiṃha, grant me the support of Your hands as I have come to the lotus-lake of Your feet (variant: as I have sought refuge in the lotus-lake of Your feet). 3.
O Abode of the World, for one fallen into the net of saṃsāra— who is like a fish caught on the hook of all sense-objects—
with his palate and head trembling violently;
O Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha, grant me the support of Your hand. 4.
O Lord, having reached this most terrible and bottomless well of saṃsāra, which is infested with the hundreds of serpents of suffering,
and being wretched and fallen at Your feet out of compassion—
O Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha, grant me the support of Your hand. 5.
O destroyer of all suffering, for one whose body is being crushed by the blows of the trunk of the terrifying elephant of saṃsāra,
and who is agitated by the fear of death and the cycle of existence;
O Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha, grant me the support of Your hand. 6.

O Śauri, whose vehicle is the enemy of serpents, whose abode is the ocean of nectar— [save me] whose form is ruined, bitten by the sharp tips of the most fierce and terrible fangs smeared with the venom of the serpent of saṃsāra!
O Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha, grant me the support of Your hand. || 7 ||

O Compassionate One, having climbed the tree of saṃsāra— which has demerit as its seed, infinite karma for its branches, the sense organs for its leaves, and the god of love for its flowers— behold it trembling, laden with the fruit of suffering.
O Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha, grant me the support of Your hand. 8.
Of one who is being swallowed by the fierce crocodiles and sea-monsters of Time within the vast ocean of saṃsāra,
whose body is overwhelmed by conflict, and who is distressed by the waves of the multitude of passions.
O Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha, grant me the support of Your hand. 9.
O Lord, O treasure-house of compassion, behold me, wretched and bewildered as I sink in the ocean of saṃsāra;
O incarnation whose sole purpose is to remove both joy and sorrow!
O Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha, grant me the support of Your hand. 10.
O Murāri, for me as I wander through the terrifying thicket of saṃsāra— afflicted by the abundance of fierce and fearsome beasts that are the Māras,
distressed, and deeply pained by the scorching heat of envy—
O Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha, grant me the support of Your hand. 11.
O Compassionate One, where the messengers of Yama, having bound me by the neck and threatening me repeatedly, drag me along while I am joined with hundreds of worldly snares—
me, alone, helpless, and terrified.
O Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha, grant me the support of Your hand. 12.

O Lord of Lakṣmī, O lotus-navelled one, O Lord of the gods, O Viṣṇu, O Lord of sacrifice, O sacrifice, O Madhusūdana, O you of universal form! O protector of the Vedas, O Keśava, O Janārdana, O Vāsudeva!
O Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha, grant me the support of Your hand. 13.
Standing with a discus in one hand, a conch shell in another, and supporting the daughter of the ocean (Lakṣmī) with yet another,
he displays the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, marked by a lotus, with his remaining left hand.
O Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha, grant me the support of Your hand.
O Lord of Gods, grant the support of Your hand to this wretched one! 14.
For me, who am blind, whose great wealth of discernment has been stolen by the thieves known as the senses— those of immense strength—
I have been cast down into the cavernous pit of the darkness of delusion.
O Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha, grant me the support of Your hand. 15.
O abode in the hearts of the foremost among the devotees of the Lord, such as Prahlāda, Nārada, Parāśara, Puṇḍarīka, Vyāsa,
and others; O Pārijāta tree for the protection of those who have taken refuge in devotion!
O Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha, grant me the support of Your hand. 16.
This auspicious hymn on earth was composed by Śaṅkara, who is like a bee at the lotus feet of Lakṣmī-Nṛsiṃha; those men who, endowed with devotion to Hari, recite it—
Thus they go to that lotus-foot of his, whose form is unimpaired. || 17 ||
[This work] is an extensive support for those submerged in the vast current of the ocean of worldly illusion, whose bodies are strengthened by that very illusion;
it is composed by the bee at the lotus feet of Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha.
This hymn, which bestows happiness upon the earth, was composed by Śaṅkara.

(17) Thus ends the *Lakṣmīnṛsiṃhakaruṇārasastotra*, the work of the venerable Śaṅkarabhagavat, the wandering ascetic teacher of the supreme order, who was the disciple of the venerable Govinda Bhagavatpūjyapāda.
